recent_posts.title: Deploy & Forget with Flatcar Container Linux (Series 5/5)
recent_posts.summary: Explore the various aspects of Flatcar Container Linux's deploy-and-forget model, including its behavior during unexpected power loss, network outages, and how it handles specialized hardware like GPUs and FPGAs. Learn about advanced topics like service mesh metrics, eBPF-based tracing, and chaos engineering to test system resilience and ensure smooth operations in diverse environments.

recent_posts.title: Assessment Methodologies: Footprinting and Scanning CTF 1 [eJPT]
recent_posts.summary: The post covers a step-by-step guide on how to find four flags in a Capture The Flag (CTF) assessment focused on footprinting and scanning skills. The methods involve using nmap for service enumeration, checking restricted directories via robots.txt, logging into an FTP server anonymously, and accessing MySQL databases using discovered credentials.

recent_posts.title: Assessment Methodologies: Information Gathering CTF 1 [eJPT]
recent_posts.summary: The post provides a detailed walkthrough of an information gathering Capture The Flag (CTF) challenge aimed at finding 5 flags. Techniques include using nmap for service enumeration, inspecting robots.txt for hidden information, directory enumeration with gobuster, searching for backup files using ffuf, and mirroring a website with httrack to uncover hidden data. Each step is methodically explained with commands and examples to guide readers through the process of identifying the flags.

recent_posts.title: Exploiting vulnerabilities in healthcare systems: A Hack The Box walkthrough
recent_posts.summary: This post explores security practices in a healthcare-focused environment by demonstrating how to exploit a medium-difficulty Linux machine named Cache. The process involves identifying vulnerabilities in OpenEMR, cracking hashed passwords, and exploiting Remote Command Execution (RCE) vulnerabilities to obtain a reverse shell. It details enumeration techniques, SQL injection attacks, and privilege escalation methods, including exploiting Docker group memberships for root access. Recommendations include upgrading software, implementing access controls, and conducting regular security assessments.

recent_posts.title: Harden Your Email Security with JohnDCyber’s SPF, DKIM & DMARC Scanner
recent_posts.summary: JohnDCyber’s SPF, DKIM & DMARC Scanner is a Python tool designed to help security engineers and IT professionals detect and remediate misconfigurations in SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records. Proper configuration of these authentication methods is crucial to prevent email spoofing, phishing, and business email compromise. The tool offers features like SPF checks, DMARC verification, DKIM confirmation, and generates comprehensive reports in CSV and HTML formats. It uses Python’s ThreadPoolExecutor for efficient scanning and supports advanced usage with various customizable flags.

recent_posts.title: Basics of cryptography ( Part1 )
recent_posts.summary: Cryptography converts readable text into unreadable ciphertext using encryption methods. Three main types include symmetric encryption (same key for encryption/decryption), asymmetric encryption (public/private key pairs), and hashing (one-way transformation for data integrity). Practical examples and websites for implementing these methods are provided.

recent_posts.title: Top 10 Web Application Security Threats
recent_posts.summary: OWASP's report on the top 10 web application security risks is widely used by global enterprises. However, Kaspersky's research, which analyzed thousands of web applications from 2021 to 2023 using various assessment methods, found significant differences. The top threats identified include broken access control, data leaks, SSRF, and SQL injection, among others. Organizations are advised to adopt flexible security measures based on impact and exploitability.

recent_posts.title: What We Learned From Salt Typhoon Telecom’s Operation
recent_posts.summary: The report by CrowdStrike reveals the advanced techniques used by the Chinese threat actor Salt Typhoon (LIMINAL PANDA) in targeting telecommunication companies. They employed methods like compromising an eDNS server using SSH password spraying, avoiding detection by focusing on non-Windows environments, and using minimal tools like the PingPong malware for persistence. Salt Typhoon also blended into network traffic using emulation tools and established multiple backdoors to maintain long-term operations across various networks.

recent_posts.title: Effective Techniques for Uncovering Origin IPs of Websites Behind WAFs
recent_posts.summary: Web Application Firewalls (WAFs) protect websites by filtering and masking the origin server's IP address. This guide outlines techniques for discovering origin IPs of websites behind WAFs, which is useful for security researchers and penetration testers. Methods include using tools like Walizer, Shodan, wwoof, and various DNS lookup and analysis techniques. The post also highlights verifying IP accessibility and automating tasks with custom scripts, emphasizing the importance of authorization and ethical practices.

top_posts.title: How to Encrypt JavaScript Code for Web Security
top_posts.summary: Encrypting JavaScript code adds a layer of protection to your website, making it harder for unauthorized individuals to understand or reverse-engineer the code. Techniques such as obfuscation and minification are commonly used, along with encryption libraries for sensitive data. Tools like SafeLine WAF can further enhance security through dynamic encryption, real-time threat detection, and zero-day protection. Combining JavaScript encryption with HTTPS and other security measures offers a comprehensive defense for your web assets.

top_posts.title: Deploy your React app using GitHub pages
top_posts.summary: Learn how to deploy your React app using GitHub Pages with easy steps. GitHub Pages is a free hosting service that allows you to easily deploy and share your web projects. Prerequisites include having a GitHub account, Git installed, and Node.js installed. Create a repository on GitHub for your React app, clone it to your local machine, and create your React app using Create React App. Add the necessary dependencies and configuration to your app, build the app, and deploy it using the 'npm run deploy' command. Commits and pushes to GitHub are also explained. Deploying to GitHub Pages is a simple and easy way to share your React app with the world.

top_posts.title: Setup SSH Keys
top_posts.summary: SSH keys provide a secure method of authenticating to remote servers, replacing traditional passwords. This tutorial covers generating an SSH key pair, copying the public key to a remote server, verifying the keys, and disabling password authentication for enhanced security.
